system_note: What was billed: Principal A40.3 (Sepsis due to Streptococcus pneumoniae) with R65.21 (severe sepsis/septic shock) and multiple MCC/CCs including J96.01, J80, I26.99; procedures include prolonged ventilation (5A1D90Z) and renal filtration (5A1D80Z billed). What the record documents and policy requires (audit rationale): 1) A40.3 (sepsis due to S. pneumoniae) and R65.21 (severe sepsis with septic shock) - supported and correctly sequenced as principal + severe sepsis: the admitting H&P documents septic shock with lactate 5.1 mmol/L and immediate vasopressor/antibiotic management and intubation (History & Physical (Admitting), History & Physical, p. 57). Infectious Diseases records confirm admission blood cultures grew Streptococcus pneumoniae (Infectious Diseases Consultation, p. 43). The governing policy for R65.21 requires provider documentation of septic shock and vasopressor + lactate criteria; those elements are present in the chart (Policy: Sepsis and Septic Shock.docx, Validation Criteria  Medical - Septic Shock Confirmed on Admission Pathway, Criterion 1 and Criterion 2). Citations: H&P (admit), ID consult, and the R65.21 policy excerpts below. 2) J96.01 (acute respiratory failure with hypoxia) and J80 (ARDS) - supported: H&P and problem lists explicitly document acute hypoxemic respiratory failure and ARDS (History & Physical (Admitting), Active Problem List, p. 57). Objective oxygenation impairment is documented repeatedly (ABGs and P/F ratios in Nephrology/RT notes; e.g., P/F 71 and P/F values <100 noted) and ARDS-specific management (low-tidal-volume ventilation, proning, neuromuscular blockade) is documented in orders and progress notes consistent with the J80 validation criteria (Critical Care Progress Note, p. 43; Respiratory Therapy Note, p. 244; Policy: J80 - ARDS Validation Criteria). These support coding of J96.01 and J80 as MCC-level conditions. 3) J95.851 (ventilator-associated pneumonia, POA = N) - supported: progress notes and ID consult document a day-6 VAP with bronchoscopy/BAL and targeted anti-pseudomonal therapy; discharge documents resolution of VAP (Critical Care Progress Note, p. 43; Infectious Diseases Consultation, p. 43; Discharge / Transfer Summary, p. 837). POA = N is correct. 4) I82.C11 (catheter-associated right IJ DVT), new atrial fibrillation (I48.91), ICU delirium (F05), critical illness myopathy (G72.81) - all supported by provider documentation and problem lists (History & Physical (Admitting) Active Problem List; Hospital Problem List, p. 344; Physician Orders documenting anticoagulation, amiodarone) and correctly flagged POA as hospital-acquired where applicable. 5) Unsupported/incorrectly coded items requiring correction: a. I26.99 (Other pulmonary embolism without acute cor pulmonale) is billed as POA = Y (MCC) but I found no provider documentation or imaging report in the retrieved chart notes diagnosing pulmonary embolism. The discharge/transfer documentation and problem lists document catheter-associated right IJ DVT and anticoagulation but do not list pulmonary embolism as a diagnosed condition at any point (Hospital Problem List, p. 344; Discharge / Transfer Summary, p. 837). Policy for I26.99 requires radiographic confirmation (CTPA/VQ) and provider diagnosis; that documentation is absent in the retrieved notes. Therefore I26.99 should be removed from the claim. b. Z99.2 (Dependence on renal dialysis) is coded POA = N on the claim but the discharge/transfer summary states renal recovery and that hemodialysis was discontinued prior to transfer (Discharge / Transfer Summary, p. 837). Z99.2 documents chronic dependence on dialysis and should not be reported when dialysis was temporary and discontinued before discharge; remove Z99.2. c. Procedure coding mismatch / missing CRRT procedure: the record documents initiation and administration of continuous renal replacement therapy (CVVHDF/CRRT) on 09/29 (Nephrology Consultation; Physician Orders show "CRRT (CVVHDF) initiation ... Administered"). The billed procedure set includes 5A1D80Z (prolonged intermittent urinary filtration <6 hours/day) but does not include a CRRT PCS code (5A1D60Z or equivalent) even though CRRT was performed and later the patient was transitioned to intermittent hemodialysis. The correct procedure reporting should include the CRRT code for the continuous therapy portion of the encounter in addition to any later intermittent dialysis code. Cite: Physician Orders (CRRT initiation - Administered) and Nephrology Consultation recommending/confirming CVVHDF. Net effect / correction summary: remove I26.99 (no clinical support in retrieved notes), remove Z99.2 (dialysis dependence resolved before discharge), and add the appropriate PCS for continuous renal replacement therapy (e.g., 5A1D60Z) to reflect the CRRT that was performed in addition to the billed intermittent hemodialysis code. Principal diagnosis A40.3 with R65.21 secondary/sequencing is supported by the documentation and may remain as billed. Key citations (see Evidence Cited section for verbatim excerpts): History & Physical (Admitting), Emergency/ICU notes, Infectious Diseases Consultation, Nephrology Consultation, Physician Orders (CRRT initiation administered), Critical Care Progress Note, Hospital Problem List, Discharge / Transfer Summary, and the governing policy excerpts for R65.21, J96.01, and J80 that establish required validation criteria.
rationale_letter: Re: Clinical validation and correction of DRG coding for inpatient claim MR_25 Dear Provider / Health Information Management Team, We completed an administrative medical record review of the above-referenced admission (admit 09/27/2026, transfer 02/06/2027). The review compared the billed diagnosis and procedure list to the documentation in the medical record and to the applicable coding policy standards. The record supports many billed diagnoses and procedures; however, we identified unsupported coding that requires correction. Finding: Removal of unsupported pulmonary embolism code and removal of dialysis-dependence status; addition of CRRT procedure code. Basis for Finding (selected supporting facts): - The admission and ICU documentation establish sepsis due to Streptococcus pneumoniae with septic shock: lactate 5.1 mmol/L, vasopressor initiation, and provider documentation of septic shock and organism identification (History & Physical (Admitting), p. 57; Infectious Diseases Consultation, p. 43). These meet the R65.21 policy criteria for severe sepsis/septic shock when paired with an organism-specific A40.- sepsis code. Therefore A40.3 and R65.21 are supported as billed. - The record documents acute hypoxemic respiratory failure and ARDS with supporting oxygenation measurements and ARDS-directed management (low-Vt ventilation, proning), satisfying the J96.01 and J80 validation criteria (Critical Care Progress Note, p. 43; Respiratory Therapy Note, p. 244; Policy: J80 - ARDS Validation Criteria). - Infectious Diseases and ICU progress notes document ventilator-associated pneumonia (day 6) with BAL and targeted therapy for Pseudomonas; discharge documents the VAP as resolved - supporting the J95.851 (VAP) code as hospital-acquired (Critical Care Progress Note, p. 43; Infectious Diseases Consultation, p. 43; Discharge / Transfer Summary, p. 837). Unsupported elements requiring correction: 1) I26.99 (Other pulmonary embolism without acute cor pulmonale) - removed. Although the claim contained I26.99, the retrieved chart notes do not include a provider diagnosis of pulmonary embolism nor a confirmatory imaging report (CTPA or V/Q) or radiology result that would meet the I26.99 validation criteria. The clinical documentation instead shows a catheter-associated right internal jugular DVT and anticoagulation without any PE diagnosis (Hospital Problem List, p. 344; Discharge / Transfer Summary, p. 837). Per policy, I26.99 requires radiographic confirmation and provider diagnosis; absent those elements, the code is not supportable. 2) Z99.2 (Dependence on renal dialysis) - removed. The discharge/transfer summary explicitly documents renal recovery and that hemodialysis was discontinued prior to transfer (Discharge / Transfer Summary, p. 837). Z99.2 denotes ongoing dependence on dialysis and should not be reported when dialysis was temporary and discontinued before discharge. 3) Procedure coding correction - add continuous renal replacement therapy (CRRT) PCS. Nephrology consultation and physician orders document initiation and administration of CVVHDF/CRRT on 09/29/2026 (Nephrology Consultation, p. 677; Physician Orders, p. 475). The claim's procedure list included an intermittent urinary filtration/hemodialysis code (5A1D80Z) but omitted a CRRT PCS (e.g., 5A1D60Z) for the continuous therapy actually performed. The CRRT procedure code should be added to accurately reflect performed services; the intermittent dialysis PCS may also remain to reflect subsequent therapy after transition. Correction applied to claim MR_25: - Remove diagnosis codes: I26.99, Z99.2 - Add procedure code: 5A1D60Z (Continuous renal replacement therapy / CVVHDF) in addition to the existing intermittent dialysis code to reflect both phases of renal replacement therapy documented in the record. If you disagree with this determination or have additional documentation (radiology report showing CTPA confirming PE, or a physician note diagnosing PE, or documentation demonstrating chronic dialysis dependence present at discharge), please provide it for reconsideration. Sincerely, Clinical Documentation Review / Audit Team

evidence_cited.excerpt: In the ED the patient met criteria for septic shock with a lactate of 5.1 mmol/L that failed to clear after a 30 mL/kg balanced crystalloid bolus. Given profound hypoxemic respiratory failure and depressed mental status the patient underwent rapid-sequence intubation, and broad-spectrum antimicrobials and vasopressor support were initiated.
